text:
emma: heads up — noticed a sudden egress cost bump in the billing export for last 48h, looks like S3 -> external region transfers for the model-archive bucket. Anyone seen this? :eyes:
raj: hmm, which bucket and approximate volume?
emma: bucket=redwood-model-archive, billing export shows ~3.2 TB/day of NETWORK_EGRESS labeled as cross-region. link: https://console.cloud.google.com/billing/... (redacted)
raj: can you paste the BigQuery breakdown? run this against billing export:
```sql
SELECT service, sku_description, SUM(cost) cost, SUM(usage_amount) bytes
FROM `billing.gcp_export`
WHERE sku_description LIKE '%Egress%' AND DATE(_PARTITIONTIME) >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 2 DAY)
GROUP BY service, sku_description
ORDER BY cost DESC
```
emma: pasted top lines: NETWORK_EGRESS to ASIA-PAC 1.8 TB, CROSS-REGION (US->EU) 1.1 TB, STORAGE_TRANSFER 0.3 TB.
infra-bot: automated-alert: cost-spike detected on tag:team=eng-infra for resource=aws:s3:redwood-model-archive (spike +410% 24h).
taylor: fwiw we rolled out a change to model-archiver last week to replicate checkpoints to eu-central for compliance snapshots. The job should only run once per version though.
oliver: could be retry loop or missing marker — if the checkpoint marker isn't updated the archiver can re-copy full objects each run. check the job logs.
raj: grabbing arhciver logs now — `kubectl logs -l app=model-archiver -n infra | grep archive | tail -n 100`
raj: logs show lots of 200s but also repeated uploads of the same prefixes with different timestamps. looks like multipart uploads finishing but the lock file isn't created.
emma: the lifecycle rules also had a cross-region replication rule added by automated terraform target: `replicate_to_eu = true` — I wonder if both replication and archiver are firing causing double copies 

oliver: snapshot of replication config from infra repo:
```hcl
resource "aws_s3_bucket_replication_configuration" "model_archive" {
  role = "arn:aws:iam::...:role/replication"
  rule {
    id = "replicate-checkpoints"
    status = "Enabled"
    destination { bucket = "arn:aws:s3:::redwood-model-archive-eu" }
    filter { prefix = "checkpoints/" }
  }
}
```

emma: yep that's the terraform rule. the archiver also copies to eu directly using `aws s3 cp --recursive` which would also incur egress if the source is in a different region.
taylor: root cause theory: terraform replication + archiver job both copying same objects = N copies * object size => huge egress. also some retries due to missing lock file.
raj: confirmed duplicated object keys in S3 inventory: grep shows ~120k objects duplicated across us-west-2 -> eu-central-1 within 24h.
infra-bot: note: cross-region replication in AWS is charged as egress from source region. estimate: 3.2 TB * $0.09/GB ~ $288/day.
emma: immediate mitigation: 1) pause archiver cron 2) disable terraform replication rule (set status=Disabled) 3) add lock/marker to archiver to avoid re-copying 4) file a postmortem and tag costs to ENGINFRA-342
raj: paused the archiver cron (k8s cronjob suspended). disabling replication via a quick terraform change now — will run plan+apply with a comment.
oliver: also we should add a cheap guard: before copying, check s3 inventory or `aws s3api head-object` to avoid overwriting; and set `--metadata-directive REPLACE` only when necessary.
taylor: long term: prefer replication OR archiver, not both. For compliance snapshots we should rely on replication with object-level checksums and replicate only on version tag. archiver should be fallback only.
emma: action items:
- raj: follow up with PR to infra repo to disable replication (temporary) and add tf guard rule (ENGINFRA-342)
- taylor: update archiver to write a done/lock file and dedupe uploads (small PR)
- oliver: run cost allocation to charge back to product teams and submit support case to AWS to double-check egress pricing anomalies
- infra-bot: create slack alert for daily cross-region egress > 500GB

raj: created ticket ENGINFRA-342 and assigned to @taylor and @oliver, added cost numbers and traces.
emma: nice, after pausing we should see drop in the next 6-8 hours as in-flight copies finish. keep eyes on billing export. :thumbsup:
oliver: one more: consider using intra-cloud network (VPC peering / AWS Transfer Family with inter-region backbone) for large transfers to reduce egress costs if this pattern repeats.

emma: thanks all — will post follow-up once 24h delta confirms mitigation.
taylor: on it.
infra-bot: note: scheduled cost-scan report will run in 2 hours.
